No bug that would make the result meaningless. Class weighting is a valid change. Because the two models' predictions are combined by scaled rank averaging, any change in probability calibration from reweighting does not distort the AUROC-based loss.

The numbers are consistent. The candidate's 0.0959 is worse than the incumbent's 0.0893 by 0.0066. With noise sd 0.0049, one candidate run and two incumbent runs, the standard error is 0.0049*sqrt(1+1/2) ≈ 0.0060, so z ≈ -1.10. The harness gave -1.094; the gap is rounding in the reported means. Rejecting is appropriate, though one run cannot tell a real harm from noise (|z| ≈ 1.1).
